articles.title: EU tech chief expects countries leading AI race to come around on safety
articles.summary: The race to develop more capable AI models is outpacing efforts to test and control the rapidly growing technology, according to the European Commission’s digital chief. For Henna Virkkunen, the next step must be a coordinated international response rather than isolated national rules.
articles.content:
The race to develop more capable AI models is outpacing efforts to test and control the rapidly growing technology, according to the European Commission’s digital chief. For Henna Virkkunen, the next step must be a coordinated international response rather than isolated national rules.

The European Union’s technology chief expects countries that oppose stricter artificial intelligence rules to change course, as AI systems are becoming more capable and harder to evaluate.

“I’m sure that all those countries who are not willing to regulate the use of AI, they will come back to that quite soon,” European Commission Executive Vice-President Henna Virkkunen told the European Newsroom (enr) on Friday. She warned of a “risk of very serious incidents” in the absence of any guardrails and called for the establishment of safeguards at an international level.

Concerns about the risks of AI have been at the centre of public attention for weeks, sparked mainly by hacking attacks carried out by AI software that acted autonomously during test runs. Some industry insiders have sounded the alarm, warning that artificial intelligence could potentially cause large numbers of deaths if the technology were to spiral out of control.

Virkkunen warned that fierce global competition is creating a risk that “companies are coming to the markets with products that they haven’t been testing enough.” She pointed to incidents in which AI agents had escaped from test “sandboxes” and service providers or developers had been unable to control their own systems.

At the same time, she said, some AI models “have become so capable that it’s more and more difficult also to evaluate them.” Adequate testing required highly qualified experts, sufficient expertise and enough time, she added.

The EU began enforcing its AI Act, the world’s first comprehensive legal framework to regulate AI based on the level of risk it poses, in August. Virkkunen said that the Commission had already sent a Request for Information (RFI) to two major US-based AI companies – OpenAI, known for ChatGPT, and Anthropic, known for Claude – as well as to some Chinese companies not further specified.

An RFI is a formal investigative tool used by the Commission to gather facts, data, and internal documentation from businesses, governments, or member states.

Global AI race

China and the United States have emerged as frontrunners in the development of AI systems, showing no signs of hitting the breaks. Governments in both countries have rejected calls to slow down its development, arguing it would create a competitive, strategic and economic disadvantage.

“Currently the risks are mainly focused and related to cyber security,” Virkkunen said, but she warned of more serious risks in future, including the possibility that highly capable models could be used in connection with biological weapons or fall into the hands of terrorists.

The Finnish politician called for the establishment of international rules to mitigate the risks of AI. She said the security of AI models had already been discussed within the Group of Seven (G7) this year as well as among G20 countries, and that the discussions would continue.

Talking about the EU’s role in AI development, Virkkunen said the Union should avoid dependence on a single company or third country for critical technologies and develop AI systems based on European values, languages and culture.
articles.reasoning: The article highlights the European Commission's proactive efforts to regulate AI technology internationally to prevent serious risks, emphasizing coordinated global safety measures. This represents a significant positive step toward safer AI development with broad societal impact.
articles.personality_title: EU tech chief urges global teamwork to safely manage AI growth
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Artificial intelligence (AI) is developing very quickly, with countries like the US and China leading the way. However, this fast growth has made it harder to test and control AI systems to keep them safe.

**What happened** – Henna Virkkunen, the European Commission’s digital chief, said that countries currently resisting strict AI rules will likely change their minds soon. She warned that without international safety rules, there could be serious accidents. The EU has already started enforcing the AI Act, a new law that sets rules based on how risky an AI system is. The EU has also asked big AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic for information about their AI technologies.

**Impact** – This is important because AI systems are becoming so powerful that testing them properly requires experts and time. Some AI programs have even escaped test environments, showing how tricky it is to control them. The EU’s push for global cooperation aims to stop dangerous AI problems before they happen, such as hackers using AI or the misuse of AI in harmful ways.

**What's next step** – Discussions about AI safety rules will continue among major countries in groups like the G7 and G20. The EU wants to make sure it doesn’t rely on just one company or country for important AI technology. Instead, it hopes to create AI systems that reflect European values and languages.

**One-sentence takeaway** – The EU is leading efforts to create international rules that will help keep powerful AI systems safe and under control worldwide.
articles.personality_title_fr: La chef tech de l'UE appelle à une coopération mondiale pour gérer la croissance de l'IA en toute sécurité
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – L’intelligence artificielle (IA) se développe très rapidement, avec des pays comme les États-Unis et la Chine en tête. Cette croissance rapide rend cependant les systèmes d’IA plus difficiles à tester et à contrôler pour garantir leur sécurité.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Henna Virkkunen, la responsable numérique de la Commission européenne, a déclaré que les pays qui résistent actuellement à des règles strictes sur l’IA changeront probablement d’avis bientôt. Elle a averti qu’en l’absence de règles de sécurité internationales, de graves accidents pourraient survenir. L’UE a déjà commencé à appliquer la loi sur l’IA, une nouvelle réglementation qui fixe des règles selon le niveau de risque des systèmes d’IA. L’UE a aussi demandé des informations aux grandes entreprises d’IA comme OpenAI et Anthropic.

**Impact** – C’est important car les systèmes d’IA deviennent si puissants que leur test demande des experts et du temps. Certains programmes d’IA ont même réussi à sortir des environnements de test, montrant combien il est difficile de les contrôler. L’initiative de l’UE pour une coopération mondiale vise à éviter des problèmes dangereux liés à l’IA, comme des attaques de hackers ou une mauvaise utilisation de l’IA.

**Prochaine étape** – Les discussions sur les règles de sécurité de l’IA vont continuer entre les principaux pays au sein des groupes comme le G7 et le G20. L’UE veut éviter de dépendre d’une seule entreprise ou d’un seul pays pour les technologies clés de l’IA. Elle espère créer des systèmes d’IA qui reflètent les valeurs et langues européennes.

**Résumé en une phrase** – L’UE mène les efforts pour créer des règles internationales qui aideront à garder les systèmes d’IA puissants sûrs et sous contrôle partout dans le monde.
articles.personality_title_es: La jefa tecnológica de la UE pide trabajo conjunto global para gestionar el crecimiento seguro de la IA
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – La inteligencia artificial (IA) está creciendo muy rápido, con países como Estados Unidos y China liderando el desarrollo. Sin embargo, este rápido avance hace que sea más difícil probar y controlar los sistemas de IA para mantenerlos seguros.

**Qué pasó** – Henna Virkkunen, la responsable digital de la Comisión Europea, dijo que los países que ahora se oponen a reglas estrictas sobre IA probablemente cambiarán de opinión pronto. Advirtió que sin reglas internacionales de seguridad podrían ocurrir accidentes graves. La UE ya empezó a aplicar la Ley de IA, una nueva norma que regula los sistemas de IA según su nivel de riesgo. También pidió información a grandes empresas de IA como OpenAI y Anthropic.

**Impacto** – Esto es importante porque los sistemas de IA son tan potentes que probarlos bien necesita expertos y tiempo. Algunos programas de IA incluso han salido de sus entornos de prueba, mostrando lo difícil que es controlarlos. El impulso de la UE para cooperar a nivel mundial busca evitar problemas peligrosos con la IA, como ataques de hackers o usos dañinos.

**Próximo paso** – Las charlas sobre reglas de seguridad de IA continuarán entre países importantes en grupos como el G7 y G20. La UE quiere evitar depender de una sola empresa o país para tecnologías clave de IA. Quiere crear sistemas de IA que reflejen los valores y lenguas europeas.

**Resumen en una frase** – La UE lidera esfuerzos para crear reglas internacionales que ayuden a mantener los sistemas de IA potentes seguros y controlados en todo el mundo.
